mainTopic: Lessons from חנה's prayer and her meeting with עלי
overview: This amud learns many lessons from the story of חנה's prayer and her meeting with עלי. רבי אלעזר teaches that you must rebuke improper behavior, clear yourself when falsely suspected, appease and bless someone you wrongly suspected, and that praying drunk is like עבודה זרה, proven from the word בליעל. The גמרא then explains words in חנה's prayer: she was the first to call ה׳ 'צבאות', and a parable of a poor man at a king's feast shows her argument. Her doubled words 'אם ראה תראה' are read as a threat to become a סוטה. That leads to the argument between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא about what the תורה promises an innocent סוטה, ending with דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם. Next come the three 'אמתך' (נדה, חלה, הדלקת הנר) and four views of 'זרע אנשים'. From חנה's later words we learn not to sit near someone davening, and we hear how young שמואל ruled הלכה before עלי and was saved by his mother. The amud ends with teachings on fasting on שבת and on חנה and אליהו speaking boldly toward Heaven. The proof that ה׳ agreed with אליהו comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the lesson: one must rebuke improper behavior
steps.stepSummary: The end of רבי אלעזר's teaching, learned from עלי: one who sees something improper in a friend must rebuke him.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...an improper matter must rebuke him.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a sentence from the previous section. רבי אלעזר learned from עלי, who scolded חנה when he thought she was drunk, that if you see your friend doing something improper, you must rebuke him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עלי thought חנה was drunk and told her so directly. Even though he was wrong about the facts, his reaction teaches a rule: when you see real wrongdoing, staying quiet is not enough, and you must speak up.

keyTerms.meaning: To rebuke him, to correct him

phrases.english: a matter that is not proper,
must rebuke him.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ הָגוּן, צָרִיךְ לְהוֹכִיחוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי אלעזר's derivation from עלי's words, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who sees improper behavior in a friend is obligated to rebuke him.

steps.title: First reading of 'No, my master': you are not a master in this matter
steps.stepSummary: עולא (or רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא) explains that חנה was telling עלי he lacked רוח הקודש, since he suspected her falsely.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And חנה answered and said: No, my master.' עולא, and some say רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, said: She said to him: You are not a master in this matter, and רוח הקודש does not rest on you, since you suspect me of this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes חנה's answer to עלי and explains the hidden meaning of the words 'No, my master.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, 'לא אדוני' just means 'No, sir.' The דרשה reads it as 'Not a master': in this matter עלי was not acting as a true leader, because a person with רוח הקודש would have known she was innocent.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say: another opinion about who said it

phrases.english: 'And Hannah answered and said: No, my master.'
phrases.notes: שמואל א 1:15

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר עוּלָּא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Ulla said, and some say Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Hanina:
She said to him:
You are not a master in this matter,
and the Divine Spirit does not rest upon you,
since you suspect me of this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next פסוק in the story, חנה's reply to עלי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'לא אדוני' means: you are not acting as a master here, because רוח הקודש is not with you.

steps.title: Second reading: 'Aren't you a master?' as a question
steps.stepSummary: A second version reads חנה's words as a question: Aren't you a leader with רוח הקודש? Why did you judge me guilty and not innocent?
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say she said this to him: Aren't you a master? Aren't the שכינה and רוח הקודש with you, that you judged me guilty and did not judge me innocent? Didn't you know that I am a woman of troubled spirit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different way of reading 'No, my master.' Here חנה asks עלי a pointed question instead of making a statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first reading, חנה says עלי lacks רוח הקודש. In this reading she says he has it, so he should have known better. Her complaint is that he judged her for the worse instead of giving her the benefit of the doubt, when he could have seen she was simply in pain.

keyTerms.meaning: For the better: giving the benefit of the doubt

phrases.english: Some say she said this to him:
Are you not a master?

phrases.aramaic: לָאו אִיכָּא שְׁכִינָה וְרוּחַ הַקּוֹדֶשׁ גַּבָּךְ,
phrases.english: Are the Divine Presence and the Divine Spirit not with you,
that you judged me guilty
and did not judge me innocent?
Did you not know
that I am a woman of troubled spirit?!
phrases.notes: This takes its words from the rest of the same פסוק: 'I am a woman of troubled spirit.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי, הָכִי אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another reading of the same words explained in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חנה was asking: If you have רוח הקודש, how could you judge me for the worse and miss that I was distressed?
steps.confusionAlert: Both versions explain the same two words, 'לא אדוני.' The first reads them as a statement (you are not a master). The second reads them as a question (aren't you a master?).

steps.title: One who is falsely suspected must clear himself
steps.stepSummary: From חנה saying 'I have not drunk wine,' רבי אלעזר learns that a person suspected of something he did not do must tell the other person he is innocent.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And wine and strong drink I have not drunk.' רבי אלעזר said: From here we learn that one who is suspected of something that is not true must let the other person know.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next words in חנה's answer. רבי אלעזר learns a practical rule from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנה did not just stay quiet, knowing in her heart that she was innocent. She told עלי clearly that she had not been drinking. רבי אלעזר learns from this that a falsely suspected person should clear his name out loud.

keyTerms.meaning: From here: introduces a lesson learned from a פסוק

phrases.english: 'And wine and strong drink I have not drunk.'
Rabbi Elazar said:
From here we learn, regarding one suspected of something not true of him,
that he must inform him.
phrases.notes: 'Him' means the person who suspects him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מִכָּאן לַנֶּחְשָׁד בְּדָבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues through חנה's reply, now drawing a הלכה from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who is falsely suspected must inform the suspecting person of his innocence.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule of behavior. Knowing you are innocent is not enough; you should also remove the suspicion from others' minds.

steps.title: Praying while drunk is like serving idols
steps.stepSummary: From חנה's words 'Do not take your maidservant as a בת בליעל,' רבי אלעזר teaches that a drunk person who prays is like one who serves עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Do not take your maidservant as a wicked woman (בת בליעל).' רבי אלעזר said: From here we learn that a drunk person who prays is as if he serves עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next פסוק, and רבי אלעזר states a strong rule about praying drunk. The proof for it comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנה was suspected of praying drunk, and she answered that this would make her a 'בת בליעל.' So praying drunk must be something that earns that harsh name. רבי אלעזר says it is as bad as עבודה זרה, and he will prove it from the word בליעל.

keyTerms.meaning: Your maidservant: a humble way of saying 'me'

phrases.aramaic: ״אַל תִּתֵּן אֶת אֲמָתְךָ לִפְנֵי בַּת בְּלִיָּעַל״.
phrases.english: 'Do not take your maidservant as a wicked woman.'
phrases.notes: שמואל א 1:16. Literally, 'Do not put your maidservant before a בת בליעל.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
From here we learn that a drunk person who prays
is as if he worships idols.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מִכָּאן לְשִׁכּוֹר שֶׁמִּתְפַּלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching of רבי אלעזר, from the next פסוק in חנה's reply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A drunk person who prays is considered as if he served עבודה זרה.

steps.title: The proof: the word בליעל links to idol worship
steps.stepSummary: A גזרה שווה: the word בליעל appears here and also with the עיר הנדחת, where it is about idol worship. So here too it points to idol worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written here: 'before a בת בליעל,' and it is written there: 'Men, sons of בליעל, have gone out from among you.' Just as there it is about עבודה זרה, so too here it is about עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now proves רבי אלעזר's rule from step 5. It compares the same word, בליעל, in two different פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In דברים, 'בני בליעל' are the men who lead a city to serve idols. Since the same word is used for חנה's case of praying drunk, the גמרא learns that this sin is compared to עבודה זרה. This method of linking two places by a shared word is called a גזרה שווה.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as there, so too here: the pattern of a גזרה שווה
A lesson learned by linking the same word in two פסוקים

phrases.english: It is written here: 'before a wicked woman,'
and it is written there:
'Wicked men have gone out from among you.'
phrases.notes: דברים 13:14

phrases.english: Just as there it refers to idol worship,
so too here it refers to idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתִיב הָכָא: ״לִפְנֵי בַּת בְּלִיַּעַל״, וּכְתִיב הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the scriptural proof for רבי אלעזר's rule in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's rule that praying drunk is like עבודה זרה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזרה שווה on the word בליעל, linking שמואל א 1:16 to דברים 13:14 (the עיר הנדחת).
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר learns three lessons from the עלי and חנה story: rebuke improper behavior, clear yourself when falsely suspected, and know that praying drunk is like עבודה זרה. The last one is proven through the shared word בליעל.

steps.title: One who wrongly suspects another must make peace and bless him
steps.stepSummary: From עלי's reply to חנה, רבי אלעזר learns that someone who falsely suspected another must appease him and also bless him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And עלי answered and said: Go in peace.' רבי אלעזר said: From here we learn that if you suspect someone of something they did not do, you must make peace with them. And more than that, you must bless them, as it says: 'And the God of Israel will grant your request.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר reads עלי's answer to חנה as a model. Once עלי learned he was wrong about her, he made peace with her and blessed her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two parts to the lesson, and each comes from a different piece of the פסוק. 'Go in peace' teaches that you must appease the person. 'May the God of Israel grant your request' teaches the extra step of giving a blessing. This is the other side of Step 4: there, the innocent person must speak up, and here, the one who suspected must fix the harm.

keyTerms.meaning: To appease him, to make peace with him
And not only that, but even more
Your request, what you asked for

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule about how people treat each other. Saying sorry is not enough. Someone who wrongly suspected another person should also wish them well.

phrases.english: "And Eli answered and said: Go in peace,"
phrases.notes: שמואל א 1:17

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
From here we learn that one who suspects his fellow
of something that is not true of him
must appease him.
And not only that, but he must also bless him.
As it is said:
"And the God of Israel will grant your request."
phrases.notes: This is the rest of the same פסוק, so עלי's blessing comes right after 'Go in peace.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מִכָּאן לַחוֹשֵׁד אֶת חֲבֵרוֹ בְּדָבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of lessons רבי אלעזר draws from the conversation between עלי and חנה. This one comes from עלי's side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who falsely suspects another must appease him and also bless him.

steps.title: חנה was the first to call ה׳ צבאות
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says that from the time the world was created, no one called ה׳‎ 'צבאות' until חנה did.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And she made a vow and said: ה׳ צבאות.' רבי אלעזר said: From the day ה׳ created His world, no person had called Him 'צבאות,' until חנה came and called Him 'צבאות.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the opening words of חנה's prayer. רבי אלעזר points out that she used a name for ה׳ that no one had used before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר makes a new claim: the name 'צבאות' starts with חנה. This step only tells us that she was first. The next step explains why she chose this name.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow, a promise to ה׳
Hosts, armies; a name of ה׳ meaning 'Lord of Hosts'
The Holy One, Blessed be He

phrases.english: "And she made a vow and said: Lord of Hosts,"
phrases.notes: שמואל א 1:11

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: מִיּוֹם שֶׁבָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶת עוֹלָמוֹ,
phrases.english: From the day that the Holy One, Blessed be He, created His world,
there was no person who called
the Holy One, Blessed be He, "Hosts,"
until Hannah came
and called Him "Hosts."

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וַתִּדֹּר נֶדֶר וַתֹּאמַר ה׳ צְבָאוֹת״, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the עלי conversation and opens a new topic about the name חנה used in her prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חנה was the first person in history to call ה׳‎ 'צבאות'.

steps.title: Why חנה called ה׳ צבאות
steps.stepSummary: חנה's point: out of all the huge hosts You created, is it hard for You to give me just one son?
steps.simpleTranslation: חנה said before ה׳: Master of the world, out of all the many hosts You created in Your world, is it hard in Your eyes to give me one son?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר explains what חנה meant by using the name 'צבאות.' She was using it to make her request.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'צבאות' means 'hosts,' all the countless creations ה׳ made. חנה sets that huge number next to her small request for a single son. Her argument is that for Someone who created so much, one more child is nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it hard in Your eyes?

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה חַנָּה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: Hannah said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the world,
out of all the hosts upon hosts
that You created in Your world,
is it hard in Your eyes
to give me one son?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרָה חַנָּה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the meaning behind the new name introduced in Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חנה used the name צבאות to argue that giving her one son is tiny compared to all of ה׳'s creations.

steps.title: Parable of the poor man at the king's feast
steps.stepSummary: A parable shows חנה's argument: a poor man pushes his way to the king and asks whether one slice of bread from his whole feast is too much to give.
steps.simpleTranslation: A parable: What is this like? It is like a human king who made a feast for his servants. A poor man came and stood at the door and said to them: Give me one slice! They paid no attention to him. He pushed his way in to the king and said to him: My master the king, out of this whole feast you made, is it hard in your eyes to give me one slice?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a story to make חנה's argument easy to picture. The poor man is like חנה, and the feast is like all of ה׳'s creations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The poor man asks for something tiny compared to the huge feast, just as חנה asks for one son out of all the hosts. When the servants ignore him, he goes straight to the king. In the same way, חנה turns directly to ה׳ with the name that shows how much He has made.

keyTerms.meaning: A parable, a story used to explain an idea
Flesh and blood, meaning a human being

steps.whatToRemember: חנה's prayer teaches a way of asking: point to how great ה׳'s giving already is, and show that your request is small next to it. The name 'צבאות' and the parable of the king's feast both make this point.

phrases.english: A parable: to what is this similar?
To a flesh and blood king
who made a feast for his servants.

phrases.aramaic: בָּא עָנִי אֶחָד וְעָמַד עַל הַפֶּתַח,
phrases.english: A poor man came and stood at the door.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: תְּנוּ לִי פְּרוּסָה אַחַת!
phrases.english: He said to them: Give me one slice!
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the king's servants at the feast.

phrases.english: And they paid no attention to him.
He pushed and went in to the king.
He said to him: My master the king,
out of this whole feast that you made,
is it hard in your eyes
to give me one slice?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָשָׁל לַמָּה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates חנה's argument from Step 9 with a parable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Asking for something small from Someone who has given so much is a strong way to make a request.

steps.title: Reading the doubled words 'If You will surely see'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the doubled verb in חנה's prayer hides two options: if You look at me now, good; if not, You will end up seeing.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the words "אם ראה תראה", רבי אלעזר said: חנה said before ה׳, 'Master of the world, if You look at me now, good. And if not, You will see.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why חנה's prayer says the word 'see' twice. רבי אלעזר splits the doubled word into two separate options.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first word (ראה) means 'if You look at me now on Your own, that is good.' The second word (תראה) means 'if not, You will be made to see me anyway.' What she means by 'You will see' is explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'seeing, You will see,' a doubled verb

phrases.english: "If You will surely see"
phrases.notes: שמואל א 1:11. The Hebrew says 'see' twice, and that doubling is what רבי אלעזר is explaining.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה חַנָּה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: Hannah said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the Universe,
"if You see" me now, good;
and if not, "You will see."

steps.triggerLanguage: אם ראה תראה אמר רבי אלעזר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי אלעזר's series of readings of חנה's prayer, moving to the next words of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The doubled 'see' means: if You grant my request on Your own, good; if not, You will be made to see me.

steps.title: חנה's plan: becoming a suspected wife to force the תורה's promise
steps.stepSummary: חנה says she will hide away with another man, be made to drink מי סוטה, be found innocent, and then the תורה's promise 'she shall conceive' must come true for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: I will go and hide away with another man in front of אלקנה my husband. Since I hid away, they will make me drink מי סוטה. You will not make Your תורה false, since it says, 'she shall be cleared and shall have children.'
steps.whatsHappening: This explains what 'You will see' means. חנה describes a plan that would make the תורה's own promise require ה׳ to give her a child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wife who was warned and then went into hiding with another man must drink מי סוטה. If she is innocent, the תורה says 'ונקתה ונזרעה זרע'. חנה, who would really be innocent, argues that ה׳ would have to keep that promise and give her a child.

keyTerms.meaning: I will hide myself away (be alone with another man)
The special water a suspected wife drinks to test her
She shall be cleared and shall have children

steps.confusionAlert: חנה is not planning to actually sin. Her plan only works because she would be completely innocent and pass the test.
steps.whyThisMatters: The whole rest of this section asks whether this plan would really work. That depends on what 'ונזרעה זרע' actually promises.

phrases.english: I will go and hide myself away
phrases.notes: She means alone with another man, which is what brings on the סוטה test.

phrases.english: before Elkana my husband,
and since I hid myself away,
they will make me drink the sota water,
and You will not make Your Torah false,
as it says: "she shall be cleared and shall conceive seed."
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:28

steps.triggerLanguage: אלך ואסתתר בפני אלקנה בעלי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the 'or else' (תראה) from step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חנה would force the Torah's promise to an innocent סוטה to give her a child.

steps.title: The plan only works if the promise means a barren woman gets a child
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: this fits the view that an innocent barren סוטה will have children, but what about the view that the promise only means easier and better births?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says that if she was barren she will have children. But for the one who says that if she used to give birth in pain she will now give birth easily, if she had daughters she will have sons, if dark children then fair ones, if short then tall, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר's reading. It points out that there is an opinion that would make חנה's plan useless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנה's plan only helps if 'ונזרעה זרע' promises children to a woman who had none. One opinion says it only improves the births of a woman who already has children, so a barren woman would gain nothing. The גמרא answers in steps 17–18: by that view, the doubled 'אם ראה תראה' teaches nothing special, because דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well for the one who says
A woman who cannot have children
What is there to say? (a challenge)

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says:
if she was barren she is remembered — that is fine;
but according to the one who says,

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיְתָה יוֹלֶדֶת בְּצַעַר יוֹלֶדֶת בְּרֶיוַח,
phrases.english: if she used to give birth in pain, she now gives birth with ease,
if daughters, she now gives birth to sons,
if dark children, she now gives birth to fair ones,
if short, she now gives birth to tall ones,
what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: הניחא למאן דאמר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the plan described in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's reading that חנה could force a child through the סוטה test.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'ונזרעה זרע' only improves the births of women who already have children, a barren woman like חנה gains nothing from the test, so her threat means nothing.

steps.title: Source of the dispute: רבי ישמעאל says a barren woman will have children
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: רבי ישמעאל learns from the פסוק that an innocent סוטה who was barren will be granted children.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'She shall be cleared and shall have children' teaches that if she was barren, she will have children. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא where the two opinions it just mentioned come from. First comes רבי ישמעאל's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל's reading is the one that fits חנה's plan, since by his view a barren woman who passes the test has children.

phrases.english: As it was taught:
"She shall be cleared and shall conceive seed" —
this teaches that if she was barren, she is remembered;
these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.triggerLanguage: דתניא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source of the two opinions named in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a תנא who holds a barren innocent סוטה is granted children.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי ישמעאל on במדבר 5:28.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's objection: every barren woman would do this
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא argues that if רבי ישמעאל were right, all barren women would hide away with other men just to be tested and then have children.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: If so, all barren women will go and hide away, and whoever did not sin will have children.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא attacks רבי ישמעאל's reading by showing what it would lead to in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the test brings children to barren women, it becomes a reward for suspicious behavior. That makes no sense, so רבי עקיבא rejects the reading. This is the same move חנה was planning.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: אִם כֵּן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him: If so,
all the barren women will go and hide themselves away,
and any one who did not sin will be remembered.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה רבי עקיבא אם כן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי ישמעאל's reading quoted in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's reading that a barren innocent סוטה is granted children.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This reading would encourage every barren woman to hide away with other men on purpose, which cannot be what the Torah intends.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's reading: better births, not children for the barren
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא explains that the promise only means that an innocent סוטה's future births will be easier and better: with ease, tall, fair, and twins.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it teaches that if she used to give birth in pain, she will now give birth easily. If short children, then tall ones. If dark, then fair. If one, then two.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives his own meaning for 'ונזרעה זרע'. This is the opinion behind the challenge in step 13. Steps 17–18 explain how this view reads חנה's doubled words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this reading the promise only improves the births of a woman who already has children. So a barren woman like חנה would not gain a child from the test, which is exactly the problem raised against רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר's reading of חנה's threat works smoothly by רבי ישמעאל. By רבי עקיבא, who says the promise only means better births, the doubled 'אם ראה תראה' is not a hint to the סוטה plan. It is ordinary speech (steps 17-18).

phrases.english: Rather, it teaches

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם הָיְתָה יוֹלֶדֶת בְּצַעַר — יוֹלֶדֶת בְּרֶיוַח,
phrases.english: that if she used to give birth in pain, she now gives birth with ease;
if short children, she gives birth to tall ones;
if dark ones, she gives birth to fair ones;
if one, she gives birth to two.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא מלמד שאם היתה יולדת בצער
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רבי ישמעאל's reading in step 15, רבי עקיבא offers his own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'ונזרעה זרע' promises an innocent סוטה easier and better births, not children for a barren woman.

steps.title: What does the doubled 'אם ראה תראה' teach according to רבי עקיבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if hiding away does not bring children, how does רבי עקיבא explain חנה's doubled words?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי עקיבא, what is learned from the doubled words 'אם ראה תראה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a quick question: how does רבי עקיבא explain the double wording in חנה's prayer? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (Step 12), the doubled words 'אם ראה תראה' were read as חנה's plan to hide away and drink מי סוטה. But רבי עקיבא holds an innocent סוטה is not promised children, so that reading doesn't work for him. So the גמרא asks what the doubling means in his view.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If You will surely see', a doubled verb in חנה's prayer

phrases.english: What is meant by 'If You will surely see'?
phrases.notes: שמואל א 1:11. Literally 'if seeing You will see'; the verb is doubled, and that's what the גמרא is asking about.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״אִם רָאֹה תִרְאֶה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows רבי עקיבא's view in Step 16 and asks how it handles the doubled words used in Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי עקיבא explains the doubled verb 'ראה תראה' if he rejects the hiding-away reading.

steps.title: The תורה speaks in the normal language of people
steps.stepSummary: The doubling is just normal speech style and teaches nothing extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה spoke in the ordinary language of people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the doubled words are just the normal way people talk, so no special lesson comes from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא does not need to find a hidden meaning in every doubled word. People often say things twice for emphasis, and the תורה uses that same style. So the doubling does not have to mean 'if not, I'll hide away'.

keyTerms.meaning: The תורה spoke in the ordinary language of people, so extra or doubled words need not teach something new

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי עקיבא, 'אם ראה תראה' is just normal emphatic speech, because דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם.

phrases.english: The Torah spoke in the language of people.
phrases.notes: He means the doubling is just normal emphasis, like people talk, so we don't learn anything extra from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּבְּרָה תּוֹרָה כִּלְשׁוֹן בְּנֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17, and so resolves the challenge of Step 13. By רבי עקיבא, the doubled verb teaches nothing extra, so there is no hint of the סוטה plan.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The doubled verb is ordinary human speech style and does not support a special דרשה.

steps.title: חנה says 'Your maidservant' three times
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes three phrases from חנה's prayer that each use the word 'אמתך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The affliction of Your maidservant', 'do not forget Your maidservant', 'and You will give Your maidservant'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lines up three phrases from the same פסוק, each with the word 'Your maidservant'. This is setting up the next step, which explains why the word appears three times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is explained yet; the גמרא just points out a pattern. One mention of 'Your maidservant' would have been enough, so the repetition invites a question.

keyTerms.meaning: Your maidservant; חנה's humble way of referring to herself

phrases.english: 'The affliction of Your maidservant.'
phrases.notes: שמואל א 1:11. All three phrases come from this one פסוק.

phrases.english: 'Do not forget Your maidservant.'
'And You will give Your maidservant.'

steps.triggerLanguage: ״בָּעֳנִי אֲמָתֶךָ״. ״אַל תִשְׁכַּח אֶת אֲמָתֶךָ״. ״וְנָתַתָּה לַאֲמָתְךָ״.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new phrase in חנה's prayer, the threefold 'אמתך'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק uses the word 'אמתך' three times, setting up a דרשה.

steps.title: The three מצוות חנה never broke
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: the three 'maidservants' match three מצוות special to women, and חנה says she kept them all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: Why these three 'maidservants'? חנה said to הקדוש ברוך הוא: Master of the world, You created three areas in a woman where she is tested for death (some say: three things that bring death close). They are נדה, חלה, and lighting the candle. Did I ever break even one of them?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא asks why 'Your maidservant' is said three times, and answers: חנה was hinting to three מצוות for women and saying she kept all three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each 'אמתך' stands for one of the three מצוות: נדה, חלה, and הדלקת הנר. These are areas where a woman can be judged harshly if she fails. חנה uses them as her argument: 'I was careful in all of them, so I deserve to be answered.' There are two versions of the wording: בדקי מיתה (tests that can lead to death) or דבקי מיתה (things that cling to death).

keyTerms.meaning: Tests of death; areas where a woman is judged and can be punished with death
Things attached to death; a second version of the same phrase
The laws of a woman's monthly separation
The portion of dough separated and given to a כהן

steps.whyThisMatters: This drasha matches the well-known משנה in שבת that names these same three מצוות as areas where women are especially judged, and it shows חנה basing her prayer on her own careful observance.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina said:
Why these three 'maidservants'?

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה חַנָּה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: Hannah said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the world,
You created three tests of death in a woman,
phrases.notes: Literally 'checks of death': areas where a woman is examined, and failing could bring a death punishment.

phrases.english: And some say: three things attached to death.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן: נִדָּה, וְחַלָּה וְהַדְלָקַת הַנֵּר.
phrases.english: And these are they: נדה, חלה, and lighting the candle.
Did I ever transgress even one of them?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: שָׁלֹשׁ אֲמָתוֹת הַלָּלוּ לָמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the threefold 'אמתך' quoted in Step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three 'אמתך' correspond to נדה, חלה and הדלקת הנר; חנה argued she had kept all three.

steps.title: The next phrase: 'offspring of men'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'זרע אנשים' from חנה's prayer to begin explaining it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And You will give Your maidservant offspring of men.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next words of חנה's prayer. This is setting up an explanation of what 'offspring of men' means, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No explanation is given yet. The unusual phrase 'זרע אנשים' (literally 'seed of men') begs the question of what kind of child חנה was asking for.

keyTerms.meaning: Offspring of men; literally 'seed of men'

phrases.english: 'And You will give Your maidservant offspring of men.'
phrases.notes: שמואל א 1:11. The explanation of 'offspring of men' comes right after this.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וְנָתַתָּ לַאֲמָתְךָ זֶרַע אֲנָשִׁים״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next phrase of the same פסוק, opening a new דרשה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quotes 'זרע אנשים' as the next text to be explained.

steps.title: What does 'offspring of men' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what חנה meant when she asked for 'זרע אנשים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'an offspring of men' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the phrase 'זרע אנשים' from חנה's prayer means. This question sets up a list of different answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every child is in some sense 'an offspring of men', so the phrase seems to add nothing. The גמרא assumes חנה was asking for something specific and wants to know what it was.

keyTerms.meaning: An offspring of men, a phrase from חנה's prayer
What is / what does it mean

phrases.english: What is 'an offspring of men'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״זֶרַע אֲנָשִׁים״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the phrase quoted in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly חנה was asking for with the words 'זרע אנשים'.

steps.title: רב: an outstanding man
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that חנה asked for a son who would stand out among men.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: a man among men.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the first answer: חנה prayed for a son who would be special and outstanding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reads 'אנשים' as meaning real, important men. חנה was not just asking for any child. She wanted a great one.

keyTerms.meaning: A man among men, someone who stands out

phrases.english: Rav said:
A man among men.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: גַּבְרָא בְּגוּבְרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in step 22.

steps.title: שמואל: a son who anoints two kings
steps.stepSummary: שמואל the אמורא explains that חנה asked for a son who would anoint two men, שאול and דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: an offspring who anoints two men. And who are they? שאול and דוד.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer: the word 'אנשים' (men, plural) hints at two specific men her son would anoint as kings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל reads the plural 'אנשים' as pointing to two people. Her son, שמואל הנביא, would later anoint both שאול and דוד as kings.

keyTerms.meaning: Anoints, pours oil to make someone king
The first two kings of ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: The אמורא named שמואל who says this is a different person from שמואל הנביא, חנה's son, whom the prayer is about.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
An offspring who anoints two men,
And who are they? Saul and David.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: זֶרַע שֶׁמּוֹשֵׁחַ שְׁנֵי אֲנָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer from רב's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'אנשים' refers to the two kings her son would anoint.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a son equal to משה and אהרן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that חנה asked for a son as great as two men, משה and אהרן, and brings a פסוק that puts them together.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: an offspring who is equal to two men. And who are they? משה and אהרן. As it says: 'משה and אהרן among His כהנים, and שמואל among those who call His name.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third answer: the 'two men' are משה and אהרן, and her son would be equal to both of them. A פסוק from תהלים backs this up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like שמואל, רבי יוחנן reads 'אנשים' as two people, but in a different way. To him the son is as great as the two greatest men, not someone who acts on two men. The פסוק lists שמואל in one line with משה and אהרן, which shows he was on their level.

keyTerms.meaning: The two great leaders of the generation of the desert
As it is said, introducing a פסוק

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
An offspring who is equal to two men,
And who are they? Moses and Aaron.
As it is stated:
"Moses and Aaron among His priests,
and Samuel among those who call His name."
phrases.notes: תהלים 99:6

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: זֶרַע שֶׁשָּׁקוּל כִּשְׁנֵי אֲנָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer. It also reads 'two men', but in a different way from שמואל.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Her son would equal משה and אהרן, as the פסוק in תהלים shows.

steps.title: רבנן: a son who blends in among people
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן explain that חנה asked for a son who would not stand out, but would blend in among people.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן say: 'an offspring of men' means an offspring who is swallowed up among men.
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth answer, going the opposite way from רב: חנה asked for an ordinary-looking son who blends in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answers read 'אנשים' as a sign of greatness. The רבנן read it as 'like everyone else'. She wanted a son with nothing odd about him that would make people stare.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
"An offspring of men": an offspring who is blended in among men.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן אָמְרִי: זֶרַע שֶׁמּוּבְלָע בֵּין אֲנָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth answer, opposite in spirit to רב's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She asked for a son who would not stand out.

steps.title: רב דימי spells out what 'blending in' means
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי lists the ways the son should be average: not too tall or short, thin or fat, pale or red, smart or foolish.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: not too tall and not too short, not too small and not too fat, not too white and not too red, not too smart and not too foolish.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי explains the רבנן's view in detail by listing pairs of extremes the son should avoid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not add a new opinion. He fills in what 'blended in' means. The son should be in the middle in looks, body, and mind, so nothing about him draws attention.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came, usually from ארץ ישראל to בבל

steps.whatToRemember: There are four views on 'זרע אנשים': a great man (רב), a son who anoints שאול and דוד (שמואל), a son equal to משה and אהרן (רבי יוחנן), and a son who blends in (רבנן, explained by רב דימי).

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
Not too tall and not too short,
and not too small and not too fat,
and not too white and not too red,
and not too smart and not too foolish.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אֲמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the רבנן's answer in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blending in means being average in height, size, color, and intelligence.

steps.title: Don't sit within four אמות of someone davening
steps.stepSummary: From חנה's words 'I am the woman who stood here with you', רבי יהושע בן לוי learns that you may not sit within four אמות of a person who is davening.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I am the woman who stood with you here.' רבי יהושע בן לוי said: from here we learn that it is forbidden to sit within four אמות of תפלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a later פסוק, where חנה brings שמואל to עלי. רבי יהושע בן לוי learns a practical הלכה from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנה says עלי was 'standing' with her while she davened. That shows עלי did not sit down near her. From this we learn that you may not sit within four אמות of someone in the middle of davening.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical הלכה: you should not sit down right next to someone who is davening שמונה עשרה.

phrases.english: "I am the woman who stood with you here,"
phrases.notes: שמואל א 1:26

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
From here we learn that it is forbidden to sit
within four cubits of prayer.
phrases.notes: He means within four אמות of a person who is davening.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: מִכָּאן שֶׁאָסוּר לֵישֵׁב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new פסוק in the חנה story and learns a הלכה from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is forbidden to sit within four אמות of someone who is davening.

steps.title: שמואל ruled הלכה in front of his teacher
steps.stepSummary: On חנה's words 'for this boy I prayed', רבי אלעזר teaches that young שמואל ruled הלכה in front of his teacher עלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For this boy I prayed.' רבי אלעזר said: שמואל was someone who ruled הלכה in front of his teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next פסוק and brings רבי אלעזר's surprising statement about young שמואל. The proof comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנה stresses 'this boy', which hints that something had happened with him. רבי אלעזר says שמואל did something serious: he ruled הלכה in front of his רבי, עלי. The proof and the reason this matters come next.

keyTerms.meaning: Rules on הלכה, gives a halachic decision

steps.confusionAlert: Ruling הלכה in front of your own רבי is a serious wrong. רבי אלעזר is not praising שמואל here.

phrases.english: "For this boy I prayed."
phrases.notes: שמואל א 1:27

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Samuel was one who ruled on halakha
in front of his teacher.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: שְׁמוּאֵל מוֹרֵה הֲלָכָה לִפְנֵי רַבּוֹ הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next פסוק and opens a new teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Young שמואל ruled הלכה in front of עלי.

steps.title: The פסוק that shows it: slaughtering the bull
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר brings a פסוק as proof: 'They slaughtered the bull and brought the boy to עלי.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'They slaughtered the bull, and they brought the boy to עלי.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר quotes the פסוק that is his source. It puts the slaughtering of the bull right next to bringing the boy to עלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting these two events side by side suggests that one caused the other. The גמרא will build on this link to show what שמואל did.

keyTerms.meaning: עלי the כהן גדול, שמואל's teacher

phrases.english: As it is stated:
"And they slaughtered the bull,
and they brought the boy to Eli."
phrases.notes: שמואל א 1:25

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיִּשְׁחֲטוּ אֶת הַפָּר וַיָּבִיאוּ אֶת הַנַּעַר אֶל עֵלִי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי אלעזר's statement in step 29.
steps.raayaObject: That שמואל ruled הלכה in front of עלי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל א 1:25, which joins the bull's slaughter to bringing the boy to עלי.

steps.title: Why would slaughtering lead to bringing the boy?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out how strange the פסוק is: why would slaughtering the bull be the reason to bring the boy to עלי?
steps.simpleTranslation: Because 'they slaughtered the bull', they brought the boy to עלי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the פסוק links the two events. This question sets up the story that comes next, which explains what שמואל did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering a bull has no clear tie to bringing a child to the כהן גדול. The question shows that something must have happened at the slaughter that involved שמואל. That event will turn out to be his ruling in front of עלי.

phrases.english: Because "they slaughtered the bull,"
they brought the boy to Eli?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּ״וַיִּשְׁחֲטוּ אֶת הַפָּר״ הֵבִיאוּ הַנַּעַר אֶל עֵלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out what is strange in the פסוק from step 30, to open the explanation.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What link between the slaughter and bringing the boy explains why the פסוק joins them.

steps.title: What really happened: שמואל says a non-כהן may slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers its question. עלי told people to call a כהן to slaughter. שמואל saw them searching and said that slaughter by a non-כהן is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, עלי said to them: Call a כהן to come and slaughter. שמואל saw them looking for a כהן to slaughter, and he said: Why are you looking for a כהן to slaughter? Slaughter by a non-כהן is valid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question from step 31 by filling in the story that the פסוק hints at. The bull's slaughter is mentioned because a ruling about that slaughter is what got שמואל brought to עלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seemed to make no sense, because slaughtering a bull is no reason to bring a child to עלי. The answer is that a question came up about who may slaughter it. שמואל gave a ruling on that question, and that ruling is why he was brought to עלי.

phrases.english: Rather, Eli said to them:
Call a priest; let him come and slaughter.
Samuel saw them
that they were searching for a priest to slaughter,
He said to them: Why do you need
to search for a priest to slaughter?
Slaughter by a non-priest is valid!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אָמַר לָהֶן עֵלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31 by supplying the hidden story behind the פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the פסוק link slaughtering the bull to bringing the boy to עלי?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A question came up about who may slaughter the bull. שמואל ruled that a non-כהן may do it, and that ruling is why he was brought to עלי.

steps.title: עלי asks שמואל for his source
steps.stepSummary: שמואל is brought to עלי, who asks him how he knows this הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought him before עלי. עלי said to him: From where do you know this?
steps.whatsHappening: עלי asks שמואל to show where his ruling comes from. This sets up שמואל's proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עלי is not attacking the ruling yet. He only wants to hear the source.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know this?

phrases.english: They brought him before Eli.
He said to him: From where do you know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא לָךְ הָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of שמואל's ruling in step 32.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source showing that a non-כהן may slaughter a קרבן.

steps.title: שמואל's proof from the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: שמואל points out that the תורה does not say 'the כהן shall slaughter.' The כהנים are mentioned only from receiving the blood onward, so slaughter may be done by a non-כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Is it written 'and the כהן shall slaughter'? It is written 'and the כהנים shall bring.' From receiving the blood onward is the job of כהנים. From here we learn that slaughter is valid by a non-כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers עלי's question with a careful reading of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, the slaughter is described without naming a כהן. The כהנים appear only at the next stage, receiving the blood. That shows the כהן's special job starts at קבלה, so slaughter comes before it and is open to a non-כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Receiving the blood of the קרבן in a bowl
A job only כהנים may do

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a real הלכה: שחיטה of a קרבן is valid even when done by a non-כהן.

phrases.english: He said to him: Is it written
"And the priest shall slaughter"?!
"And the priests shall bring" is written,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:5. That פסוק mentions the slaughter first without naming any כהן, and only then mentions the כהנים bringing the blood.

phrases.english: from receiving the blood onward it is a מצוה of priests,
from here we learn that slaughter is valid by a non-priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי כְּתִיב ״וְשָׁחַט הַכֹּהֵן״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers עלי's request for a source in step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק names the כהנים only from קבלה onward, so slaughter does not need a כהן.

steps.title: Right on the הלכה, but wrong to rule before his teacher
steps.stepSummary: עלי agrees that שמואל is correct. But anyone who rules הלכה in front of his teacher deserves death.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You have spoken well. But you are ruling הלכה in front of your teacher, and anyone who rules הלכה in front of his teacher is liable to death.
steps.whatsHappening: עלי accepts the ruling but condemns the way it was given. This step shows the actual point of רבי אלעזר's teaching from step 29.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being correct is not enough. Ruling in front of your teacher shows disrespect, so the problem is about respect for the teacher, not about whether the ruling is true.

keyTerms.meaning: Ruling הלכה in front of one's teacher

steps.confusionAlert: עלי is not saying שמואל's ruling was wrong. The ruling was correct; the problem was giving it in front of his teacher.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source of the well-known rule that a student may not rule הלכה in front of his teacher.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מֵימָר שַׁפִּיר קָא אָמְרַתְּ,
phrases.english: He said to him: You have spoken well,

phrases.aramaic: מִיהוּ מוֹרֶה הֲלָכָה בִּפְנֵי רַבָּךְ אַתְּ,
phrases.english: but you are ruling halacha in front of your teacher,
and anyone who rules halacha in front of his teacher
is liable to death.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵימָר שַׁפִּיר קָא אָמְרַתְּ, מִיהוּ מוֹרֶה הֲלָכָה בִּפְנֵי רַבָּךְ אַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts שמואל's proof from step 34 but objects to the act of ruling in front of a teacher.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who rules הלכה in front of his teacher is liable to death, even when his ruling is correct.

steps.title: חנה saves her son: 'For this boy I prayed'
steps.stepSummary: חנה cries out to עלי. עלי offers to pray for an even greater son, but חנה insists she prayed for this boy.
steps.simpleTranslation: חנה came and cried out before him: 'I am the woman who stood here with you.' He said to her: Let me punish him, and I will pray for mercy, and ה׳ will give you one greater than him. She said to him: 'For this boy I prayed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with חנה protecting שמואל. This shows why she said 'for this boy I prayed' (step 29).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her words 'for this boy' mean she wants this child and no other, even one who is greater. This closes the explanation of the פסוקים that רבי אלעזר started in step 29.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל ruled correctly that a non-כהן may slaughter, but he deserved punishment for ruling in front of עלי. חנה saved him by insisting 'for this boy I prayed.'

phrases.english: Hannah came and cried out before him:
"I am the woman who stood here with you, etc."
phrases.notes: שמואל א 1:26. She is reminding עלי that this child came from her prayers.

phrases.english: He said to her: Let me punish him,
and I will pray for mercy,
and He will give you one greater than him.
She said to him: "For this boy I prayed."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָתְיָא חַנָּה וְקָא צָוְוחָה קַמֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to עלי's death sentence in step 35 and closes the story.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'For this boy I prayed' means חנה wanted this very child spared, and she refused a replacement.

steps.title: חנה's prayer 'on her heart': nothing in a woman was created for nothing
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי יוסי בן זמרא explains 'she spoke על לבה' as 'about matters of her heart.' She argued that every body part has a purpose, so her breasts should be used to nurse a son.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And חנה spoke on her heart.' רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי יוסי בן זמרא: about matters of her heart. She said: Master of the World, You created nothing in a woman for no purpose. Eyes to see, ears to hear, a nose to smell, a mouth to speak, hands to work, feet to walk, breasts to nurse. These breasts You placed on my heart, why? Not to nurse? Give me a son and I will nurse with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to חנה's prayer and explains an unusual phrase in the פסוק, 'על לבה' (on her heart).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'על' is read as 'about,' so she prayed about the body parts on her heart, her breasts. Her argument is that ה׳ made nothing in vain, so these too must be used for their purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: About the matters of her heart

phrases.english: "And Hannah, she spoke on her heart."
phrases.notes: שמואל א 1:13. The phrase "on her heart" sounds odd, and that is what the גמרא is explaining.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן זִמְרָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Yosei ben Zimra:
About the matters of her heart.
She said before Him: Master of the World,
of all that You created in a woman,
You did not create one thing for nothing:
eyes to see, and ears to hear,
a nose to smell, a mouth to speak,
hands to do work with,
feet to walk with,
breasts to nurse with.

phrases.aramaic: דַּדִּים הַלָּלוּ שֶׁנָּתַתָּ עַל לִבִּי לָמָּה?
phrases.english: These breasts that You placed on my heart, what are they for?
Is it not to nurse with them?!
Give me a son, and I will nurse with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וְחַנָּה הִיא מְדַבֶּרֶת עַל לִבָּהּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the פסוקים about חנה's prayer and explains a new phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'על לבה' means חנה prayed about her breasts, arguing that ה׳ created nothing in vain.

steps.title: Fasting on שבת: a decree is torn up, but he is punished for missing עונג שבת
steps.stepSummary: Also from רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי יוסי בן זמרא: one who fasts on שבת has a seventy-year decree torn up. Even so, he is later held accountable for not having delight on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי יוסי בן זמרא: Anyone who fasts on שבת has his decree of seventy years torn up. Even so, they come back and punish him for the מצוה of enjoying שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a side teaching only because it comes from the same speakers as the last step. It is not connected to חנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fasting on שבת has two results. It is powerful enough to cancel a harsh decree. But it still cancels the מצוה of עונג שבת, so the person must answer for that too.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן זִמְרָא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Yosei ben Zimra:
Anyone who sits in a fast on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: קוֹרְעִים לוֹ גְּזַר דִּינוֹ שֶׁל שִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה.
phrases.english: they tear up for him his decree of seventy years.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן חוֹזְרִין וְנִפְרָעִין מִמֶּנּוּ
phrases.english: And even so, they come back and punish him
for the law of delight of Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן זִמְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side teaching added because it shares the same speakers as step 37.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fasting on שבת tears up a seventy-year decree, yet the person is still punished for missing עונג שבת.

steps.title: What is the fix for fasting on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a person who fasted on שבת can repair the problem of missing שבת delight.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is his remedy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question that sets up the next step: what can a person who fasted on שבת do to fix it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 38 said the faster's bad decree is torn up, but he is still held accountable for missing עונג שבת. So the natural question is how he can clear that remaining problem.

phrases.english: What is his remedy?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי תַּקַּנְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the punishment mentioned in Step 38.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can someone who fasted on שבת repair the loss of עונג שבת?

steps.title: Fast again to make up for the שבת fast
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that he should observe another fast to atone for the fast on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: He should sit in a fast for the fast.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives the fix: the person should fast another time to make up for having fasted on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that a fast took away שבת delight. The fix is a second fast, done on a weekday when fasting is allowed, as atonement for the first.
steps.whatToRemember: Someone who fasted on שבת makes up for it with another fast on a weekday.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
He should sit in a fast for the fast.
phrases.notes: He means a second fast on a weekday to make up for the one on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: לִיתֵּיב תַּעֲנִיתָא לְתַעֲנִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 39.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He should observe an additional fast to atone for the שבת fast.

steps.title: חנה spoke boldly toward Heaven
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says חנה spoke sharply toward הקדוש ברוך הוא, learned from the unusual wording "על ה׳".
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: חנה spoke boldly toward on High, as it says "and she prayed upon ה׳". This teaches that she spoke boldly toward on High.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to חנה and brings רבי אלעזר's teaching that her prayer was bold and pointed toward Heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a פסוק would say she prayed "אל ה׳" (to ה׳). Instead it says "על ה׳" (upon ה׳), which רבי אלעזר reads as speaking pointedly toward Heaven. This fits Step 37, where she argued that her body parts must have a purpose.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
Hannah spoke boldly toward on High.
As it is stated: "And she prayed upon the Lord,"
phrases.notes: שמואל א 1:10. The usual wording would be "אל ה׳", to ה׳, so "על" stands out.

phrases.english: This teaches that she spoke boldly toward on High.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: חַנָּה הֵטִיחָה דְּבָרִים כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the חנה story after the side topic of fasting on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From "על ה׳" we learn that חנה spoke boldly toward Heaven.

steps.title: אליהו also spoke boldly toward Heaven
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says אליהו spoke sharply toward הקדוש ברוך הוא, saying that ה׳ turned the people's hearts backward.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: אליהו spoke boldly toward on High, as it says "and You turned their hearts backward".
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר brings a second example of someone who spoke boldly toward Heaven: אליהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his prayer, אליהו told ה׳ "You turned their hearts backward," as if ה׳ caused the people to sin. Saying that to ה׳ is very bold, so it fits the same pattern as חנה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
Elijah spoke boldly toward on High,
As it is stated: "And You have turned their hearts backward."
phrases.notes: מלכים א 18:37, from אליהו's prayer on הר הכרמל.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אֵלִיָּהוּ הֵטִיחַ דְּבָרִים כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel statement from the same רבי אלעזר, applying the same idea to אליהו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אליהו spoke boldly toward Heaven by saying ה׳ turned the people's hearts backward.

steps.title: How do we know ה׳ agreed with אליהו?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר רבי יצחק asks for the source showing that הקדוש ברוך הוא later admitted אליהו was right.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר רבי יצחק said: From where do we know that הקדוש ברוך הוא went back and agreed with אליהו?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמואל בר רבי יצחק asks for a source. This step only sets up the question; the answer comes in the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After hearing that אליהו's words were bold, we might think they were wrong. רבי שמואל בר רבי יצחק says the opposite: ה׳ actually agreed with him, and he is about to show where we see it.

keyTerms.meaning: and agreed with him, admitted he was right

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think אליהו was punished or rejected for his bold words. This question assumes ה׳ actually agreed with him.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַבִּי יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Rabbi Yitzḥak said:
From where do we know that the Holy One, Blessed be He, went back
and agreed with Elijah,

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן שֶׁחָזַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְהוֹדָה לוֹ לְאֵלִיָּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 42 by claiming ה׳ agreed with אליהו and asking for the proof.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that הקדוש ברוך הוא admitted אליהו was correct.
